title: Strangolapreti Trentini
subtitle: Trentino bread and spinach dumplings with browned butter and sage
excerpt: Strangolapreti are Trentino bread and spinach dumplings: a mixture of stale bread soaked in milk, spinach, egg, and Parmesan, formed into rough oval shapes and boiled. They are dressed with browned butter and sage. The name means priest-stranglers, a joking reference to a greedy priest who ate too many.
sourceNotes: Strangolapreti are a traditional dish of Trentino-Alto Adige, the Alpine region bordering Austria. They reflect the cucina povera tradition of using stale bread to make a satisfying meal. Similar dumplings appear in the Austrian and South Tyrolean tradition under various names.

content.text: Strangolapreti are one of the simplest Italian dumplings to make: the bread soaks in milk, the spinach is cooked and squeezed dry, and everything is mixed together with egg, Parmesan, and a little flour. The mixture should be firm enough to hold its shape when rolled. If too soft, add more flour. If too stiff, add a splash of milk.

items.prepNote: stale bread, crusts removed, torn into pieces

content.text: Soak {{bread-white}} bread pieces in {{whole-milk}} warm milk for 10 minutes until soft. Squeeze out as much milk as possible.

Combine the squeezed bread with {{spinach-frozen}} spinach, {{eggs}} beaten eggs, {{parmesan}} Parmesan, {{nutmeg}} nutmeg, and {{salt-table}} salt. Add {{plain-flour}} flour and mix to a firm dough. If sticky, add more flour a tablespoon at a time.
Shape the mixture into oval dumplings about 5cm long. Cook in batches in well-salted boiling water for 4 to 5 minutes until they float and have cooked through. Lift with a slotted spoon.

Brown {{unsalted-butter}} butter in a wide pan over medium heat until golden and nutty. Add {{sage}} sage leaves and crisp for 30 seconds. Add the dumplings and toss to coat. Serve with {{parmesan}} Parmesan.

items.symptom: The dumplings fall apart in the water
items.cause: The mixture is too wet, or not enough flour was used.
items.fix: Test one dumpling first. If it falls apart, mix more flour into the dough. The mixture should hold its shape when formed but still be soft. Squeeze the bread and spinach as dry as possible before mixing.

content.text: Strangolapreti are a classic dish of Trentino, the Alpine region on the Austrian border. They come from the mountain tradition of using stale bread and greens to make a filling meal. The name means priest-stranglers. A very similar dish appears in South Tyrol under the name Spinatknodel (spinach dumpling). A different dish with the same name exists in Campania -- the Trentino version is always the bread-and-spinach one.
